native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: In a logistic (log-odds) regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on race with no other covariates, the coefficient -0.9568 corresponds to Black compared to White: Black respondents have lower log-odds of completing a BA degree than White respondents (odds ratio ~0.38; MLE on this data is -1.0057, and the standard default-regularized fit gives ~-0.961).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded 8773-row NLS SES data (0 missing; 236 BA completions, 2.69%). Computed descriptive stats and 6-direction pairwise quantities (mean diffs, Cohen's d, standardized diffs, log-odds ratios). Fitted logistic regressions of BA on race with 3 reference groups x 4 covariate sets (race-only; +SES+sex; +SES+sex+ABILITY+PERCENTILE; all 5), reporting intercepts, coefficients and SEs, cross-checked against hand-computed log-odds. Matched -0.9568 at +/-0.001 then +/-0.005: no hit among unpenalized MLE specs. Extended search over all 32 covariate subsets x 3 refs (96 race coefficients), probit, OLS (raw/standardized), effect coding, PCA factor-score diffs, and an L2-regularized logit lambda scan: the value lies exactly on the shrinkage path of the Black-vs-White coefficient (lambda ~1.05-1.1 gives -0.9572, |diff| 0.0004; default C=1 gives -0.9614, |diff| 0.0046), while the Hispanic-vs-White coefficient moves away from the target under any shrinkage. Concluded Black compared to White on the log-odds scale.
